mainTopic: Why an impure vessel may not be immersed on שבת and יום טוב: four reasons (רבה, רב יוסף, רב ביבי, רבא) and the challenges to them
overview: This amud asks why an impure כלי may not be immersed on שבת and יום טוב. רבה says it is a גזירה, because a person might carry the vessel four אמות in רשות הרבים. When אביי pushes back, רבה adds that a private pit is banned because of a public pit, and יום טוב because of שבת. Several sources then seem to show that the חכמים did not make such decrees: השקה, drawing water with an impure pail, two split rulings in ברייתות, and a נדה immersing in her clothes. Each is answered in one of two ways: either the special method keeps the person aware of the rule, or the case is rare and the חכמים do not decree about rare cases. רב יוסף gives a different reason, סחיטה, and survives the same challenges with the same answers. רב ביבי says the worry is that people would delay immersing, and a ברייתא supports him. רבא says immersing looks like fixing a vessel. A person immersing himself is different, because he looks like he is cooling off. רב נחמן בר יצחק begins answering the question of dirty water, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבה's reason: he might carry the vessel in the public domain
steps.stepSummary: רבה finishes his reason: we forbid immersing a vessel on שבת because a person might carry it four אמות in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The חכמים made a decree] in case he picks up the vessel in his hand and carries it four cubits in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: We are picking up in the middle of רבה's explanation. He says the ban on immersing vessels on שבת exists so that a person will not carry the vessel through the public domain to the מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's point is that immersing a vessel is not forbidden in itself. It is a גזירה to protect the real איסור of carrying in רשות הרבים. Everything that follows tests how far this reason reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest; in case (the usual opening of a rabbinic decree's worry)
Four cubits, the distance that counts as forbidden carrying in the public domain on שבת
The public domain

steps.whyThisMatters: This reason, a worry about carrying, is the base that אביי's two questions will attack.

phrases.english: lest he pick it up in his hand
phrases.notes: This finishes רבה's sentence from just before. "It" is the impure vessel he wants to immerse.

phrases.english: and carry it four cubits in the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's explanation, which began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Immersing a vessel on שבת is forbidden by גזירה, out of worry that he will carry it four אמות in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: אביי asks: what if the pit is in his own courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה: if the person has a מקוה pit in his own courtyard, there is no worry about carrying, so why forbid it?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If he has a pit in his courtyard, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's reason. If the water is in his own private courtyard, he will never go into רשות הרבים, so the worry seems not to apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's reason only makes sense when the person must walk through public space to reach the water. אביי shows a case where that never happens, so the ban should not apply there. Yet the ban on immersing seems to cover every case.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit; here a pit of water fit to be a מקוה
A courtyard (private space)
What is there to say? (a challenge formula)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
If he has a pit in his courtyard,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי יֵשׁ לוֹ בּוֹר בַּחֲצֵירוֹ מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far רבה's reason reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reason that the ban exists because of carrying in רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When the pit is in his private courtyard there is no carrying in public, so the reason falls away.

steps.title: רבה answers: a private pit is banned because of a public pit
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the חכמים forbade even a pit in one's courtyard, so people would not confuse it with a pit in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is a decree. A pit in his courtyard is forbidden because of a pit in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends his reason by saying the חכמים made the rule the same for everyone. Even when there is no carrying, immersing is forbidden so that people do not come to immerse in a public pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה covers the safe case too, so the rule stays simple and nobody makes mistakes. The private courtyard case is not an exception to the ban. It is pulled in on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to guard against a more serious איסור
Because of; on account of (a case forbidden because of a similar case)

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is a decree: a pit in his courtyard
on account of a pit in the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ גְּזֵירָה בּוֹר בַּחֲצֵרוֹ אַטּוּ בּוֹר בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extending the גזירה to cover the similar safe case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A private pit should be allowed, since there is no carrying.
steps.terutzMaskana: The private pit is also forbidden, as a גזירה because of a public pit.

steps.title: אביי asks: what about יום טוב, when carrying is allowed?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges again: the carrying worry works on שבת, but on יום טוב carrying is allowed, so why forbid immersing then?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for שבת. But on יום טוב, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a second challenge. On יום טוב carrying between domains is permitted, so the worry about carrying does not exist at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first challenge was about one place, a private courtyard. This one is about a whole day, יום טוב. Since carrying is not forbidden then, רבה's reason seems to have nothing to protect.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for... (it accepts one case before raising a problem with another)
A Festival day, when carrying is permitted

phrases.english: This works well for Shabbat,
but on Yom Tov, what is there to say?
phrases.notes: On יום טוב carrying is allowed, so the worry about carrying doesn't fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח שַׁבָּת בְּיוֹם טוֹב מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רבה's reason, this time about יום טוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's carrying reason as applied to יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On יום טוב carrying is allowed, so a ban based on carrying should not apply.

steps.title: רבה answers: יום טוב is banned because of שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the חכמים forbade immersing on יום טוב because of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They made a decree about יום טוב because of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the same kind of answer again. יום טוב is forbidden so that people will not come to immerse on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now two layers of גזירה. Private pit because of public pit, and יום טוב because of שבת. This layering is what the גמרא will question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the חכמים) decreed

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, immersing a vessel is forbidden everywhere and on both days. The private pit is forbidden because of a public pit, and יום טוב because of שבת.

phrases.english: They decreed about Yom Tov on account of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's יום טוב challenge from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extending the גזירה from שבת to יום טוב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: On יום טוב immersing should be allowed, since carrying is permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: יום טוב is forbidden too, as a גזירה because of שבת.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: השקה is allowed even though it looks like immersion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether we really make such decrees. A משנה allows השקה of impure water on יום טוב, and does not forbid it because it looks like טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really make such decrees? But we learned: Both agree that one may bring water into contact [with מקוה water] in a stone vessel to purify it, but one may not immerse. If such decrees exist, let us decree against השקה because of טבילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole idea of stacking decrees. It quotes a משנה where השקה is allowed, even though it looks a lot like the forbidden טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים forbade one thing because of something similar, as with יום טוב because of שבת, they should also forbid השקה because it resembles הטבלה. Since the משנה allows השקה, it seems the חכמים do not make decrees like this.

keyTerms.meaning: And do we really decree? (opens a challenge)
But didn't we learn in a משנה?
Bringing impure water into contact with מקוה water so it becomes pure
A stone vessel, which cannot become impure
Immersing (here, immersing an impure vessel)

steps.confusionAlert: השקה is not itself the forbidden immersion of a vessel, because the stone vessel never becomes impure. The question here is different: since השקה looks like טבילה, why didn't the חכמים forbid it by גזירה? Step 7 answers this.

phrases.english: And do we decree [in such a case]?
But didn't we learn:
And they agree that one may bring the water into contact
phrases.notes: "They" are בית שמאי and בית הלל. The water is impure water, made to touch the מקוה water.

phrases.english: in a stone vessel to purify it,
but one may not immerse.
And if it is so —
let us decree against bringing into contact on account of immersing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method of decreeing one case because of a similar case, used in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the חכמים forbid one thing because of a similar thing (יום טוב because of שבת)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה permits השקה even though it resembles הטבלה, which shows the חכמים do not always make such decrees.

steps.title: Answer: השקה is a rare case, since he is careful with this water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a person only needs השקה when he has no other good water. Then he guards this water carefully, so its becoming impure is unusual, and no decree was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really think that? If he had other good water, why would he need to do השקה for this water? It must be that he has no other water. And since he has no other water, he is very careful with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge. השקה only comes up in an unusual situation, so it is not like immersing vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone with no other water guards this water closely, so it rarely becomes impure. Since השקה is a rare event, the חכמים did not bother decreeing against it. Immersing vessels is common, so a גזירה there makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (pushes back on the question itself)
Good water; pure water fit to drink
He is very careful

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים make decrees for common situations, like immersing a vessel. השקה is rare, because a person with no other water guards it carefully, so they did not make a decree about it.

phrases.english: And can you really think so?
If he has good water,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי לְמָה לִי לְמֶעְבַּד לְהוּ הַשָּׁקָה?
phrases.english: why do I need to do hashakah to these?
phrases.notes: "These" means the impure water he wants to purify.

phrases.english: Rather, it must be that he doesn't have [other water],
and since he doesn't have [other water],
he is very careful with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא אִי אִית לֵיהּ מַיִם יָפִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a rare case versus a common case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the חכמים decree יום טוב because of שבת, they should also decree השקה because of הטבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: השקה is unusual, since he has no other water and guards it carefully, so no גזירה was made. This does not weaken the decrees about immersing vessels.

steps.title: Challenge from drawing water with an impure pail
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא that allows drawing water on יום טוב with an impure pail, which purifies the pail. Why not forbid this too, in case the person comes to immerse the pail directly?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged רבה: A ברייתא teaches that on יום טוב you may draw water from a מקוה with an impure pail, and the pail becomes pure. If the חכמים made decrees like yours, they should forbid this too, in case the person comes to immerse the pail by itself!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's decree again. He brings a case where a vessel actually becomes pure on יום טוב and it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an impure pail is lowered into a מקוה to draw water, it is fully under the water, so it gets a real טבילה. If the חכמים worried about immersing vessels on יום טוב, they should have worried that this permitted method would lead people to immerse the pail in the normal way. Since the ברייתא allows it, it looks like there is no such decree.

keyTerms.meaning: One may draw water
A pail or bucket
Let us make a decree
By itself, in the plain normal way

phrases.english: He objected to him: One may draw water with an impure pail,
phrases.notes: This is אביי challenging רבה. The water is drawn from a מקוה on יום טוב.

phrases.english: and it becomes pure.
phrases.notes: While it is filling up, the pail is fully under the water of the מקוה, so this counts as its טבילה.

phrases.english: And if it is so, let us decree
lest he come to immerse it by itself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רבה's decree, after the answer about השקה in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the חכמים forbade immersing vessels on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא allows a pail to become pure through drawing water on יום טוב and makes no decree against it. That suggests the חכמים did not make decrees like this.

steps.title: The person remembers because it is only allowed through drawing
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the pail may only be purified by drawing water with it, so the person stays aware that a normal immersion is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there. He is only allowed to purify the pail by drawing water with it, so he remembers that he may not immerse it the normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains why drawing water with an impure pail did not need a decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The היתר only works in one special way: drawing water. Because the person must purify the pail in this unusual way, he is reminded that a regular טבילה is forbidden. So there is no real danger that he will slip into a normal immersion.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
It was permitted
He remembers

phrases.english: It is different there,
since it was permitted to him only
by means of drawing water with it,
he remembers.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא הוּתְּרָה לוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי דׇּלְיוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the special method itself prevents the mistake.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Allowing the pail to be purified this way might lead people to immerse vessels normally.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the היתר works only through drawing water, the person stays alert, and no decree was needed.

steps.title: Challenge from a vessel that became impure on יום טוב itself
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא: a vessel that became impure on ערב יום טוב may not be immersed on יום טוב, but one that became impure on יום טוב may be. Why not forbid the second because of the first?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him again: A vessel that became impure on ערב יום טוב may not be immersed on יום טוב. A vessel that became impure on יום טוב may be immersed on יום טוב. If the חכמים made decrees like this, they should forbid the יום טוב case because of the ערב יום טוב case!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a second ברייתא that allows immersing a vessel on יום טוב in one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא really does forbid immersion in one case, a vessel that became impure on ערב יום טוב. אביי argues that if the חכמים like to make protective decrees, they should also have forbidden the very similar case of a vessel that became impure on יום טוב, so people would not mix the two up.

keyTerms.meaning: The day before יום טוב
One may immerse
Because of, as a protection for

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: כְּלִי שֶׁנִּטְמָא מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: He objected to him: A vessel that became impure on the eve of יום טוב,
one may not immerse it on יום טוב;

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב — מַטְבִּילִין אוֹתוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: if it became impure on יום טוב, one may immerse it on יום טוב.
And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if the חכמים really made decrees like the one רבה described.

phrases.aramaic: נִגְזוֹר דְּיוֹם טוֹב אַטּוּ דְּעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב!
phrases.english: let us decree against the one of יום טוב because of the one of the eve of יום טוב!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: כְּלִי שֶׁנִּטְמָא מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רבה's decree, after Step 9 answered the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's approach that the חכמים made protective decrees about טבילה on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows immersion when the impurity happened on יום טוב, even though people could confuse it with the forbidden ערב יום טוב case. That suggests no such decree exists.

steps.title: Impurity on יום טוב is uncommon, so no decree was made
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that becoming impure on יום טוב rarely happens, and the חכמים do not make decrees about rare cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Becoming impure on יום טוב is something that doesn't happen often, and about something uncommon the חכמים did not make a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains why the יום טוב case was left permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה is made to protect against a situation that comes up often. Since a vessel rarely becomes impure on יום טוב itself, there was no need to forbid it. So the ברייתא does not prove that the חכמים never make decrees, only that they skip rare cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that does not happen often
They decreed
The חכמים, the Rabbis

steps.whatToRemember: A key rule: the חכמים do not make a גזירה about something that rarely happens (מילתא דלא שכיחא).
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is used all over the תלמוד to explain why the חכמים left certain cases without a protective decree. רבה will lean on it again in the next answer.

phrases.english: Impurity on יום טוב
is something that is uncommon,
and about something that is uncommon
the Rabbis did not make a decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְאָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב מִלְּתָא דְּלָא שְׁכִיחָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rare-case principle: no decree for an uncommon situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יום טוב case should have been forbidden to protect the ערב יום טוב case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since impurity on יום טוב is rare, the חכמים did not bother to decree against it.

steps.title: Challenge from a vessel made impure by a lesser source
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא: a vessel made impure by an אב הטומאה may not be immersed on יום טוב, but one made impure by a ולד הטומאה may. Why not forbid the second because of the first?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him again: A vessel that became impure from an אב הטומאה may not be immersed on יום טוב. One that became impure from a ולד הטומאה may be immersed on יום טוב. If the חכמים made decrees like this, they should forbid this one because of that one!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a third ברייתא with a split ruling, and asks why the permitted case was not forbidden too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אב הטומאה is a main source of impurity, and a ולד הטומאה is something that got its impurity from an אב. The ברייתא forbids immersing a vessel in the first case but allows it in the second. אביי asks: if the חכמים make protective decrees, why not forbid the lighter case so people don't confuse it with the stricter one?

keyTerms.meaning: A main source of impurity
Something that became impure from a main source; a secondary source of impurity
This one because of that one

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two terms: an אב הטומאה is the original, stronger source. A ולד הטומאה is its 'child,' a weaker impurity it passed on.

phrases.english: He objected to him: A vessel that became impure from a main source of impurity,
one may not immerse it on יום טוב;

phrases.aramaic: בִּוְלַד הַטּוּמְאָה — מַטְבִּילִין אוֹתוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: from a secondary source of impurity, one may immerse it on יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אִיתָא, נִגְזוֹר הָא אַטּוּ הָא!
phrases.english: And if it is so, let us decree against this one because of that one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge to רבה's decree, after Step 11 answered the second.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's approach that the חכמים made protective decrees about טבילה on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows immersing a vessel made impure by a ולד הטומאה, even though it could be confused with the forbidden אב הטומאה case. That suggests no such decree exists.

steps.title: Only כהנים care about this kind of impurity, and they are careful
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that people only bother about a vessel made impure by a ולד הטומאה when it comes to כהנים, and כהנים are careful. So this case is rare and needed no decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where would you find someone caring about impurity from a ולד הטומאה? Only with כהנים, and כהנים are careful.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains why the ולד הטומאה case was left permitted. This answers the third ברייתא; one more challenge follows in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel made impure by a ולד הטומאה only matters to someone handling תרומה, which means כהנים. Since כהנים are careful to keep their vessels pure, this kind of impurity rarely happens. So the same rule from Step 11 applies: no decree for something uncommon.

keyTerms.meaning: Where would you find it?
Priests
Careful, quick to act properly

steps.whatToRemember: All three answers protect רבה's decree. Drawing water with a pail keeps the person alert. Impurity on יום טוב is rare. Impurity from a ולד הטומאה only matters to careful כהנים. In the last two cases the rule is the same: the חכמים make no גזירה for a rare case.

phrases.english: A secondary source of impurity, where do you find it?
phrases.notes: He means: where would anyone actually bother to purify a vessel with this weaker impurity?

phrases.english: Only with regard to priests,
and priests are careful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12, using the rare-case rule from Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rare-case principle applied: the situation only comes up with careful כהנים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ולד הטומאה case should have been forbidden to protect the אב הטומאה case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only כהנים care about this impurity, and they are careful, so it is rare and no decree was made.

steps.title: A woman immersing in her clothes: why no decree?
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a נדה with no pure clothes may immerse while wearing her clothes, which purifies them too. If the חכמים made a decree against immersing vessels, why not forbid this as well, so she will not come to immerse the clothes by themselves?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: A נדה who has no pure clothes may use a trick and immerse while wearing her clothes. If there really is such a decree, we should forbid this too, so she will not come to immerse the clothes by themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to challenge רבה's decree. רב allows a woman to purify her clothes by wearing them while she immerses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Immersing clothes alone on שבת or יום טוב is forbidden by the decree. But רב lets her purify them indirectly by wearing them. If the חכמים worried so much, they should have forbidden even this indirect way, so she would not go on to immerse the clothes directly.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her state of menstrual impurity, who purifies herself by immersing in a מקוה.
Uses a trick: she reaches a permitted result in a roundabout way.
And if it is so. Meaning: if your claim is true.
By themselves, in their plain form.

phrases.english: Come and hear,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: for Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
A menstruating woman who has no (pure) clothes —
uses a trick and immerses in her clothes.
And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if רבה is right that the חכמים made a decree against immersing vessels.

phrases.english: let us decree, lest she come to immerse them by themselves!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge in the same series against רבה's decree, following the three ברייתות in steps 8–13 (the pail, ערב יום טוב, and אב/ולד הטומאה).
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that immersing vessels on שבת and יום טוב was forbidden as a protective decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the decree exists, the חכמים should also have forbidden the indirect immersion of clothes while wearing them. Since רב permits it, maybe there is no such decree.

steps.title: She will remember, because it is only allowed while wearing them
steps.stepSummary: The case is different. She may purify the clothes only by wearing them, so she stays aware that immersing them alone is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there. Since it was allowed to her only by wearing them as clothing, she remembers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The special way she must do it keeps her reminded of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing the clothes in the water is an unusual way to purify them. Because of this, she will not forget that immersing them the normal way is forbidden. This is the same idea as the pail in step 9: an unusual method keeps a person alert.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there. A standard way to show a case is not a real comparison.
A garment, something worn.
She remembers. She stays aware of the prohibition.

phrases.english: It is different there,
since it was not permitted to her
except by means of wearing them —
she remembers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the unusual method itself prevents the feared mistake.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Allowing her to immerse in her clothes shows there is no decree against immersing vessels.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree exists. Here no extra decree is needed, because the special method keeps her aware of the prohibition.
steps.whatToRemember: All the challenges against רבה's decree were answered. Each time the answer was either that the person stays aware of the rule, or that the case is rare, so no decree was needed.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the decree is because of wringing
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a different reason for forbidding immersion of vessels. People might wring out the wet items, and that is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is a decree because of wringing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives a different reason for the same rule. רבה's reason was carrying four אמות in רשות הרבים. רב יוסף's reason is סחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that immersing vessels is forbidden by a decree. They disagree only about what the חכמים were worried about. רב יוסף fears that after immersing something like clothing, a person might squeeze the water out, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree made by the חכמים to keep people from a real prohibition.
Wringing or squeezing out liquid, which is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is a decree because of wringing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: גְּזֵרָה מִשּׁוּם סְחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reason for the decree that רבה explained in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Immersing vessels on שבת and יום טוב is forbidden so that people will not come to wring them out.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not arguing about the rule itself. Everyone agrees immersing vessels is forbidden. The argument is only about why.

steps.title: What about vessels that cannot be wrung?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: wringing explains the rule for clothes, but many vessels, like metal or wood, cannot be wrung. Why are they forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: This works well for vessels that can be wrung. But for vessels that cannot be wrung, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's reason. It seems to fit only some vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule forbids immersing all vessels. If the worry is wringing, it should apply only to things that can be squeezed, like cloth. Hard vessels have nothing to wring, so the reason does not seem to cover them.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well. Used to grant one part before raising a problem with another.
Items that can be wrung, such as cloth.
What is there to say? A challenge that the reason does not cover this case.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
This works well for vessels that are fit for wringing.
Vessels that are not fit for wringing,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's reason from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reason that the decree is because of סחיטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason applies only to things that can be wrung, yet the prohibition covers all vessels.

steps.title: One rule for all vessels
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the חכמים forbade vessels that cannot be wrung because of those that can, so the rule stays the same for everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is a decree for these because of those.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his reason. The חכמים extended the decree to all vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original worry is about things that can be wrung. But to keep the rule simple and avoid mix-ups, the חכמים forbade immersing any vessel. So hard vessels are forbidden as a secondary step.

keyTerms.meaning: These because of those: forbidding one group so people will not confuse it with another.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is a decree for these because of those.
phrases.notes: "These" are the hard vessels that cannot be wrung. "Those" are things like clothes that can be.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extension of the decree: a second-level decree to keep the rule the same for everything.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wringing reason cannot explain why hard vessels are forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hard vessels are forbidden because of vessels that can be wrung, so all vessels follow one rule.

steps.title: The same challenges, the same answers
steps.stepSummary: אביי raised all his earlier challenges against רב יוסף, and רב יוסף answered them the same way רבה did.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him with all these challenges, and he answered him as we answered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up instead of repeating everything. All of אביי's earlier challenges to רבה were also raised against רב יוסף, and they got the same answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenges from steps 8–15 attack the idea of a decree, not the specific reason behind it. So they apply to רב יוסף too. The answers also work for him: the person stays aware, or the case is rare and the חכמים do not decree about rare cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A challenge or refutation from an earlier source.
As we answered: the same answers given earlier.

phrases.english: He challenged him with all these challenges,
and he answered him as we answered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ כֹּל הָנֵי תְּיוּבָתָא, וְשַׁנִּי לֵיהּ כִּדְשַׁנִּינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב יוסף's branch by applying the whole earlier back-and-forth to his reason.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both רבה and רב יוסף hold that immersing vessels on שבת and יום טוב is forbidden by a decree. The challenges against the decree are answered the same way for both: the person stays aware of the rule, or the case is rare.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה's reason is carrying four אמות. רב יוסף's reason is סחיטה. They differ about the reason, but both survive the same challenges with the same answers.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that challenges aimed at the existence of a decree apply no matter which reason is behind it.

steps.title: רב ביבי: a decree so people will not delay immersing
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי gives a new reason for the ban: if immersing vessels were allowed on יום טוב, people might put it off until then.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי said: It is a גזרה, in case a person delays.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא, רב ביבי, gives his own reason why we may not immerse a טמא vessel on שבת or יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If טבילה were allowed on יום טוב, a person might leave his טמא vessels lying around until יום טוב, when he has free time. Keeping טמא vessels at home for a long time could cause pure things to become טמא. So the חכמים banned it completely.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule the חכמים made to keep people from coming to a problem
In case he delays (puts it off)

phrases.english: Rav Beivai said:
It is a decree, lest he delay.
phrases.notes: He means a person might hold off immersing his טמא vessels until יום טוב, when he has more free time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third reason for the same ban, different from רבה and רב יוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Immersing vessels on יום טוב is forbidden so that people will not delay purifying their vessels.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב ביבי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a vessel that became טמא before יום טוב may not be immersed on יום טוב, for the same reason רב ביבי gave.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches like רב ביבי: A vessel that became טמא on ערב יום טוב may not be immersed on יום טוב, as a גזרה in case he delays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the exact same reason as רב ביבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא talks about a vessel that already became טמא before יום טוב. The owner could have immersed it earlier. Banning it on יום טוב stops him from waiting on purpose, and the ברייתא even uses רב ביבי's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא teaches in line with him (support)
The day before יום טוב
We immerse (in a מקוה to make pure)

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with Rav Beivai:
A vessel that became impure on the eve of a Festival —
one may not immerse it on the Festival,
as a decree, lest he delay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב ביבי's reason with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב ביבי's reason: a גזרה in case a person delays immersing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that uses the same words, גזרה שמא ישהא.

steps.title: רבא: it looks like fixing a vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a fourth reason: immersing a vessel looks like repairing it, which is forbidden on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Because it looks like he is fixing a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives yet another reason for the ban on immersing vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the טבילה the vessel could not be used, and after it the vessel can be used. That looks like fixing a vessel, which is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב. So the חכמים banned immersing vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixing a vessel, a forbidden act on שבת
It looks like

phrases.english: Rava said:
Because it looks as if he is repairing a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a fourth reason for the same ban.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Immersing a vessel is forbidden because it looks like fixing it.

steps.title: Then a person should also be forbidden to immerse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if טבילה looks like fixing, a person immersing himself should also be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a person too should be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's reason by pointing to a person who immerses himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא person who immerses also goes from טמא to טהור, so he is "fixing" himself in the same way. But the משנה allows a person to immerse on יום טוב. So why does רבא's reason not forbid that too?

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Also, too

phrases.english: If so, a person too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reason that טבילה looks like fixing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same logic would forbid a person from immersing, but a person is allowed.

steps.title: A person looks like he is cooling off
steps.stepSummary: A person in water looks like he is just cooling off, not purifying himself, so there is no look of fixing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person looks like he is cooling off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a person in water does not look like he is fixing anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When people see a person in water, they think he is just refreshing himself. It is not clear that he is becoming טהור, so it does not look like fixing. A vessel has no such other reason to be in the water.

keyTerms.meaning: Cooling off (refreshing himself)

phrases.english: A person looks as if he is cooling off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא against רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: a person and a vessel look different in the water.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A person immersing looks like he is fixing himself, just like a vessel.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person looks like he is cooling off, so there is no look of fixing.

steps.title: What about dirty water?
steps.stepSummary: The answer works for clean water, but nobody bathes in dirty water to cool off, so why is it allowed there?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is fine for good water. For bad water, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer by asking about a person who immerses in dirty water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person in clean water might be bathing for pleasure. Nobody bathes in murky water for pleasure, so there it is clear he is doing טבילה. Then it should look like fixing and be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for
Good, clean water
Bad, murky water
What is there to say?

phrases.english: This works well for good water;
for bad water, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תִּינַח מַיִם יָפִים, מַיִם רָעִים מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a person looks like he is cooling off.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In dirty water no one would think he is cooling off, so it should look like fixing.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק starts to explain that even in dirty water it is not clear the person is doing טבילה. His answer continues on the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Sometimes a person comes...
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins to answer the question about dirty water. The sentence is not finished yet and continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is setting up a real-life case where a person might go into even dirty water for a reason other than טבילה. If so, even dirty water does not clearly show he is purifying himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence stops in the middle. Do not try to guess the end yet; the answer is finished on the next line of the daf.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Sometimes a person comes

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: פְּעָמִים שֶׁאָדָם בָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the dirty-water question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that even dirty water does not clearly show טבילה (answer continues).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In dirty water it is clear he is purifying himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sometimes a person has another reason to go into such water (finished on the next amud).
